# Tahuna

> Open-source control and compute plane for ML workloads. Run your Python code on remote GPUs while Tahuna handles the infrastructure around it.

Tahuna is a CLI-first compute orchestration platform for ML engineers, AI researchers, and agent builders who need remote GPUs without rebuilding the surrounding infrastructure for every workload. You bring your Python code, framework, dependencies, and data; Tahuna handles code and data sync, GPU provisioning, dependency installation, run execution, log and metric streaming, artifact persistence, and compute cleanup.

Tahuna occupies the gap between managed APIs that constrain the workload and raw GPU compute that requires manual DevOps. The current public release focuses on compute orchestration. Higher-level training and inference workflows, followed by observability, are the next parts of the roadmap.

## Core workflow

1. Install the CLI and authenticate: `curl -fsSL https://tahuna.app/install.sh | bash && tahuna login`
2. Initialize a project: `tahuna init .` — writes `.tahuna/tahuna.toml`, scaffolds `train.py`, `pyproject.toml`, and `uv.lock` when missing.
3. Add credits in the dashboard billing view.
4. Launch a training run: `tahuna train` — syncs code and data, provisions a GPU pod, executes the entrypoint, streams logs and metrics, persists output artifacts.

## Key concepts

- **Environments** — Isolated compute configurations storing GPU type, GPU count, volume size, Python version, and framework. Created via `tahuna init`.
- **Runs** — A single remote execution of your code. Each run is pinned to exact code and data snapshots and captures logs, metrics, and artifacts.
- **Sync** — Incremental, content-addressed upload to R2. Only changed blobs are uploaded. Code and data syncs happen automatically before each run, and manually via `tahuna sync`.
- **Artifacts** — Output files written to the configured output directory are collected after a successful run and stored in cloud storage.
- **Experimental serving** — A trained model artifact can be promoted to an inference endpoint via `tahuna serve create --from-run <run-id>`. This interface is experimental and is not part of the current compute-orchestration release.
- **Experimental auto-research** — A bounded local experiment loop. This interface is experimental and is not part of the current compute-orchestration release.

## CLI reference

### Authentication
- `tahuna login` — Browser OAuth flow. Stores API key in `~/.config/tahuna/config.env`.
- `tahuna version` — Print CLI version.

### Project setup
- `tahuna init .` — Initialize current directory as a Tahuna project.
- `tahuna up` — Alias for `tahuna init .`.

### Training
- `tahuna train` — Sync code and data, provision GPU, run training, stream output.
- `tahuna train -d` — Detached mode: launch and return immediately.
- `tahuna train --gpu-type <gpu> --gpu-count <n> --volume-gb <n>` — Override GPU spec for the run.
- `tahuna train --warm` / `--keep-warm-minutes <n>` — Keep the pod warm after the run.

### Sync
- `tahuna sync` — Sync code and data.
- `tahuna sync code` — Sync code only.
- `tahuna sync data` — Sync data only.

### Run management
- `tahuna run list` — Show last 5 runs (newest at bottom). `-n <N>` for N runs, `-a` for all.
- `tahuna run show <run-id|name>` — Show run details, status, and artifact keys.
- `tahuna run logs <run-id|name> [--follow] [--tail <N>]` — Stream or tail run logs.
- `tahuna run metrics <run> --metric <name> [--follow]` — Stream a specific metric.
- `tahuna run watch <run-id|name>` — Poll run status until terminal.
- `tahuna run cancel <run-id|name>` — Cancel a running or queued run.
- `tahuna run rename <run-id|name> --name <new-name>` — Rename a run.
- `tahuna run rm <run-id|name|pattern>... [--all] [--cancel] [--force]` — Delete runs.

### Environments
- `tahuna env list` — List environments.
- `tahuna env show <env-id>` — Show environment details.
- `tahuna env update [<env-id>] --gpu-type <gpu> --gpu-count <n> --volume-gb <n>` — Update GPU spec.
- `tahuna env rm <env-id>` — Delete environment, runs, and artifacts.
- `tahuna env data bind <env-id> <data-id>` — Bind a data item to an environment.
- `tahuna env data unbind <env-id> <data-id>` — Remove a data binding.

### Environment variables
- `tahuna env_vars list` — List env var names for the linked environment.
- `tahuna env_vars get <name>` — Get one env var value.
- `tahuna env_vars set NAME=value` — Set an env var.
- `tahuna env_vars set --from-file <path>` — Load env vars from a `.env` file.
- `tahuna env_vars rm <name>` — Remove an env var.

### Data
- `tahuna data list` — List data items in the workspace.
- `tahuna data show <data-id>` — Show data item details.
- `tahuna gpus list` — List available GPU types and prices.

### Experimental serving
- `tahuna serve create --from-run <run-id> [--model-path <path>]` — Create a serve from a run artifact.
- `tahuna serve create --from-storage-prefix <prefix>` — Create a serve from a storage prefix.
- `tahuna serve list` — List serves.
- `tahuna serve show <serve-id>` — Show serve details.
- `tahuna serve logs <serve-id>` — Stream serve logs.
- `tahuna serve stop <serve-id>` — Stop a serve.

### Experimental auto-research
- `tahuna research run --program <file.md> --metric final:<name> --minimize|--maximize --max-trials <N> --max-spend-usd <USD> --max-trial-minutes <N> --editable <path>` — Start a bounded research session.
- `tahuna research run --resume <session-id>` — Resume a session after editing an allowed file.
- `tahuna research graph <session-id> [--output <path>]` — Render an SVG progress graph.

### Shell
- `tahuna shell` — Interactive REPL that wraps CLI commands in a persistent session.

## Configuration

Local project state lives in `.tahuna/tahuna.toml`:

```toml
[project]
entrypoint = "train.py"
data_dir = "data"
output_dir = "outputs"
python_project_file = "pyproject.toml"
uv_lock_file = "uv.lock"

[environment]
framework = "pt"
python_version = "3.11"
```

Auth and URL overrides via environment variables:
- `TAHUNA_API_KEY` — Auth token (set by `tahuna login`).
- `TAHUNA_API_URL` — API base URL override (default: `https://tahuna.app`).
- `TAHUNA_BROWSER_URL` — Browser base URL for login flow.
- `TAHUNA_CONFIG_DIR` — Config directory override (default: `~/.config/tahuna`).

## Compute and pricing

Supported GPUs (billed per active hour): L4, RTX 3090, RTX 4090, A100 (40 GB and 80 GB), H100 SXM, H100 PCIe, H200, RTX PRO 6000, B200.
Volume storage: $0.12 / GB / month.
Tahuna Cloud uses prepaid credits. Runs draw down credits for active GPU time and attached volume. No compute markup for individual users.

## Frameworks

PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Unsloth, TRL, Verifiers — and any Python entrypoint that runs from `uv run`. Python 3.11–3.14 supported via uv.

## Run lifecycle statuses

`queued` → `provisioning` → `running` → `completed` | `failed` | `cancelled`

## Tech stack

- CLI: Go
- Web and API: Next.js, Convex, Better Auth
- Runtime: Dockerized Python + uv on RunPod GPU pods
- Storage: Cloudflare R2
- Experimental inference proxy: Next.js edge route at `/api/serves/{serve_id}/inference/...`
